implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.update() advances gravity by moving the current_piece down each drop interval; pieces are created with row=0 (top of the board).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can move left/right before landing
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.move_horizontal(dx) shifts the piece when board.is_valid_position() permits; main.py maps LEFT/RIGHT keys to this method.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can rotate pieces before landing
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.rotate_piece() attempts a clockwise rotation using Tetromino.rotated_matrix() with simple wall‑kick offsets; main.py maps the UP key to this method.
Board.clear_lines() removes fully occupied rows and returns the count; Game._lock_current() calls this after locking a piece.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring increases with line clears and drops
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._lock_current() adds LINE_SCORES[cleared] * level to score; soft_drop adds SOFT_DROP_SCORE per row, hard_drop adds HARD_DROP_SCORE per row.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when no more pieces can be placed
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_game_over() checks if a newly spawned tetromino fits; Game._new_piece() sets game_over flag when it cannot.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board updates after each move or drop
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.lock_piece() writes piece cells to the grid; clear_lines() updates the grid; UI.draw() renders the current board state each frame.

implemented_requirements.requirement: All seven standard Tetromino shapes are included
implemented_requirements.evidence: settings.SHAPES defines I, O, T, S, Z, J, L; Tetromino selects from these; the 7‑bag randomizer in Game._spawn_from_bag uses the same keys.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Drop speed increases as the game progresses
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.drop_interval decreases with level (BASE_DROP_INTERVAL - (level‑1)*DROP_SPEEDUP_PER_LEVEL) and level rises based on cleared lines.

judge.summary: The provided code implements a functional Tetris core: falling pieces, player movement and rotation, line clearing, scoring, game‑over detection, all seven tetrominoes, and level‑based speed increase. The board logic, game rules, and pygame UI are present and appear syntactically correct, giving a high likelihood of successful execution.
